text:
Late in a pleasant middle, a noisy queue arose while the kennel attendant was handling it. Incident Report: Queue Disturbance During Animal Check-In. I attended the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways after travelers raised overlapping concerns about carrier handling, label checks, and the order of acceptance at the counter. The senior coordinator took control of the line, separated the callers by matter, and asked the welfare coordinator to assess each animal for stress. One traveler reported a loose latch on a carrier, and another stated that paperwork for an animal in transit had not been clearly explained at the point of handoff. The disturbance remained verbal, but the crowd pressure increased and service slowed.

I spoke with the travelers in turn and kept the desk ledger current while the kennel attendant secured the affected carrier and checked the animal inside for comfort. The senior coordinator redirected other travelers to the waiting area and kept the counter clear for essential work. <<FACT F120>> The staff then reviewed the acceptance notes, confirmed the carrier condition, and resumed handling once the animal was settled. A further review was made of the service change record so the desk log would match the actual sequence of events.

There was no injury and no property loss. The delay was caused by confusion at the front of the queue and by the need to verify the carrier before release to the next stage. <<FACT F109>> The travelers were informed of the next service step in plain terms, and the carrier remained under watch while boarding continued. I instructed staff to keep the queue spaced more clearly at the desk, to call the senior coordinator sooner when a line becomes tense, and to note any animal welfare concern before it reaches the counter. The welfare coordinator will review the incident with the kennel attendant and confirm that the handling steps used here are followed on future shifts. The desk remained operational and the matter was closed without further disruption.
